mappings.note: Identifies the Indian Ocean from the continents that hem it in - pairing an ocean with continents on the world map, which is LO-5. Not LO-6, since no latitude or longitude is quoted.

Attributes the four-to-seven spread in continent counts to cultural and historical convention, i.e. how the continents of LO-5 are divided. Not LO-2, which would apply only if the earth's spheres or life were at issue.
Requires the superlatives attached to each continent (largest, coldest, smallest, most populous) and spotting the false one - continent knowledge under LO-5.
Phytoplankton as the base of the ocean food web and a source of oxygen is squarely the biosphere that LO-2 singles out. Not LO-5: nothing is located on a map.
Why 'marine' means saltwater - a distinction between saline and freshwater environments, which belongs to the earth's water zones rather than to ocean placement.
Picks marine fauna (a blue whale) against flora distractors, so it tests animal life in the ocean - the biosphere half of LO-2, paired with the flora items.
The colour that earns the earth its 'blue planet' name, i.e. its water cover. Not LO-5, since no ocean is named.
The three-fourths water fraction - the extent of the hydrosphere. Distinct from the blue-planet colour item in asking for a quantity, but the frame offers only LO-2 for both.
One-line definition of a continent, the land category LO-5 asks pupils to place on the world map.
The Navy motto invoking Varuna is a cultural-tradition recall, so C-SST4.2 rather than a geography outcome; competency level because LO-25 demands analysis of ancient ideas, not recall of a motto.

Which hemisphere holds more water needs the world-map spread of ocean and land (LO-5) plus the Equator that defines the hemispheres (LO-6). Not LO-2, because the point is distribution, not the water's role in life.
Whether the oceans are separate or interconnected - a property of how the named oceans of LO-5 sit together on the map, not of the biosphere.
Names a source of fresh water (glacier, river, lake, groundwater) - the fresh-water component of the earth's water zones in LO-2. Not LO-7, since no Indian river has to be located.
The count of five oceans; prerequisite knowledge for labelling them on a world map.
The Pacific as the largest ocean - a size fact about the oceans of LO-5.
The Arctic as the smallest ocean; mirror of the largest-ocean item and under the same outcome, the only one naming oceans.
Defines flora as plant life, which is the biosphere named in LO-2. Not LO-5, no place is located.
Defines fauna as animal life - the animal half of the biosphere, the companion item to the flora definition.
Names the sea lying WEST of India, so it needs both a direction on a flat surface and a water body - both clauses of LO-5. Not LO-7, because the Arabian Sea is not one of India's own landforms.
Eurasia as the joined Europe-Asia landmass; a continent-division fact, hence LO-5 rather than the earth's spheres.
The seven-continent convention in common use - the counterpart of the item on WHY the count varies, and under the same outcome.
The Olympic rings as inhabited continents; a continent-count recall, so LO-5.
Defines an island as land smaller than a continent surrounded by water - the land-and-water vocabulary of LO-5.
Greenland as the largest island; a named place on the world map. Not LO-7, which is reserved here for Indian features.
Names one of India's two island groups, an Indian feature to be placed on the map of India. Not LO-5, because the item is about India rather than about the world's oceans and continents.
The name of India's first Antarctic research base is India's contribution in science, which LO-24 covers. Kept off LO-5, which is used for the item asking which continent it stands on.
Oceans as the 'planet's lungs' producing oxygen - the ocean's role in sustaining life, so LO-2. Not LO-5, no ocean is named or located.
World Oceans Day exists to press the ocean's role in life and its conservation, which is the habitability theme of LO-2. There is no outcome about awareness days, so this is the nearest honest fit.
Names a human-caused threat to marine life - damage to the biosphere, which LO-2 names. Not C-SST4.1, which is about occupations rather than environmental harm.
Explains the 'blue planet' name at three-mark length; still the water cover of the earth, so LO-2 as with the shorter versions.
How oceans and continents shape climate and so all life - the earth-as-habitat sense of LO-2, not the locating task of LO-5.
Seawater versus fresh water by usability; a property of the earth's water that decides what people and animals can drink.
Water scarcity on a water-covered planet, because the accessible fresh share is tiny - the same fresh/saline split, asked for its consequence.

Whether ocean boundaries are natural or conventional - about how the oceans of LO-5 are delimited on a map. Not LO-2, even though the answer mentions ecosystems, because the question is about the dividing lines.
Describes marine flora, algae and seaweeds, and their part in the food web and oxygen production - the biosphere of LO-2 in its fullest form in this chapter.
